note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses), review round 1, written on 18 Oct 2026 on the new device. Not yet acted on.

item-quality.verdict: The item is solvable and fair to the answers a competent developer would give, but it does not fully hold up: its oracle leaves several stated requirements unchecked. That gives two medium findings and one low. What holds: the start graph fails at V3 with exactly the stated symptom (Samples/Symbol and Taps: name 'spb' is not defined), and the fault, a deleted variable block, is realistic. Family repair and level L2 are right (11 functional blocks with a 5x rate change, QPSK modulation and RRC filtering). The instruction states every number the checks use (48 kHz, 9.6 kBd, magnitude 2, 2.5, RMS 2.0 within 5 %, from the 2,049th symbol on, rx_symbols.dat as complex) and leaks nothing beyond the symptom. GRC-Agent's inspect_graph shows the same validation errors, and change_graph can add a variable named spb. Every valid alternative I wrote passed 16 of 16 runs at 8 in parallel, with bit-identical V6 values: spb = int(samp_rate/sym_rate); spb = 5.01, literal or samp_rate/sym_rate/interpratio (compensating the offset); spb = samp_rate/sym_rate*interpratio = 4.99 (64/64); init_phase nfilts/2; and the textbook taps form with int(11*spb*nfilts). The memorised 4.2563, 4.8, 4.9 and 5.15 fail in every run. The problems: (F1, medium) 'Keep the transmitter, the channel model and all five File Sinks as they are' and the stated channel values are unchecked. Deleting four File Sinks, noise 0 or 0.15, clock offset 1.0 or 1.002 and roll-off 0.35 all pass, and with the clock offset removed, a receiver with no timing recovery passes. (F2, medium) corr_ref is phase-blind and compares only the in-phase signs, so outputs rotated by 90 or 45 degrees, or conjugated, give exactly the reference's V6 values. (F3, low) the receiver's stated 32 filters, loop bandwidth and maximum deviation are unchecked, and variant v3 (64 filters) contradicts the instruction. Probe graphs and results are in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-17/probes/ (probe_results*.json, rate_probe.json, *.ladder.json); the scripts are ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-17/probe17.py and rate17.py. I did not edit the task directory.

findings.claim: V6 does not check the instruction's last sentence ('Keep the transmitter, the channel model and all five File Sinks as they are'), nor the channel and transmitter values it states (noise voltage 0.05, timing offset 0.998, roll-off 0.5). The oracle observes only rx_symbols.dat, and none of these changes moves its three features out of range. Because the clock offset is the only thing that makes timing recovery necessary, removing it lets an answer with no timing recovery at all pass. The item's core skill can therefore be bypassed by breaking a requirement that is stated but not checked.
findings.evidence: I built probe flowgraphs from reference.grc and ran ladder.check with the task's oracle. The V6 values are corr_ref / max_abs / rms; the reference scores 0.7068 / 2.090 / 1.983. Probes that pass: tx_signal_sink and the three timing_* sinks deleted (identical values; the clock sync's outputs 1-3 are optional, so V3 passes); noise_amp 0 (0.7068 / 2.064 / 1.983); noise_amp 0.15; interpratio 1.0; interpratio 1.002 (offset reversed); rolloff 0.35 on both transmitter and receiver (0.7061 / 2.141 / 1.970). Shortcut: I deleted the Polyphase Clock Sync and its three sinks, set interpratio to 1, and put Delay(3) followed by a Decimating FIR Filter (ccf, decim 5, taps firdes.root_raised_cosine(1.0, 5, 1.0, rolloff, 221)) before rx_symbols.dat. It passes V6 under ./gb ladder (0.7071 / 2.066 / 1.999, EVM 1.1 %, better than the reference's 3.4 %; probes/shortcut_no_clock_sync_delay3.ladder.json). The same shortcut with interpratio kept at 0.998 fails for every delay from 0 to 4 (corr_ref 0.106-0.109; probes/rate_probe.json). Mutants: only the 20x and 25x violations in the mutant list (noise 1.0, interpratio 1.05) are killed. A frequency offset of 1e-5 is caught (corr_ref 0.658). The noise level cannot be measured at rx_symbols.dat: EVM is 3.2 % at noise 0 and 3.4 % at 0.05, while valid answers range from 2.7 % to 4.1 %. The mean of timing_rate.dat tracks the offset (0.0534 at 0.998, 0.0000 at 1.0, -0.0532 at 1.002), but it also depends on the receiver's filter count (v3: 0.107) and on the spb regime (spb 4.99: 0.264), so a signal check on it would reject valid variants.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the 'keep' sentence structurally, in the p2p group. (1) Add five block_present checks on blocks_file_sink, with params {file: tx_signal.dat | rx_symbols.dat | timing_error.dat | timing_rate.dat | timing_phase.dat}. (2) Add a path check from channels_channel_model via digital_pfb_clock_sync_xxx to blocks_file_sink: the receiver keeps its timing recovery, which kills the shortcut. (3) For the channel and transmitter values, either add a graph-check kind that compares evaluated parameter values (channel epsilon 0.998, noise_voltage 0.05, freq_offset 0, taps 1; resampler rrate 5; roll-off 0.5), or, as a stopgap, use block_present on channels_channel_model with params {epsilon: interpratio, noise_voltage: noise_amp, freq_offset: freq_offset} plus block_present on variable with params {value: 0.998} and {value: 0.05}. Then add the surviving mutants (see compliance F1) and re-run the gates. If the team instead drops the 'keep' sentence and the values that cannot be verified, the path check is still needed to exclude the shortcut.

findings.claim: The instruction asks that the recovered symbols 'be the transmitted symbol sequence ... without rotation ..., each sitting on its QPSK point'. The only check on this is corr_ref, which compares against the signs of the in-phase parts of the transmitted symbols and takes the magnitude of the complex correlation. It is therefore blind to any constant phase rotation and never looks at the quadrature half of each symbol; max_abs and rms do not depend on phase either. Three wrong outputs pass with exactly the reference's values: rotated by 90 degrees (every symbol on a different QPSK point), rotated by 45 degrees (every symbol halfway between two QPSK points), and complex-conjugated (I/Q mirror: the Q bit of every symbol inverted). The check note says 'a slip, a rotation or a different symbol sequence gives 0.03-0.66', but that holds only for a rotation that drifts over time, i.e. a frequency offset.
findings.evidence: ./gb ladder with the task's oracle (probes/*.ladder.json). Multiply Const 1j inserted between the clock sync and rx_symbols.dat: V6 passes with corr_ref 0.706775, max_abs 2.090434 and rms 1.98332, bit-identical to the reference. Multiply Const exp(j*pi/4): the same values, and it passes, although the error to the nearest QPSK point is 75 % of the symbol magnitude (reference 3.4 %). Complex Conjugate inserted: the same values, and it passes, although its correlation with the complex transmitted symbols is 0.04 (reference 0.9994). Channel taps 1j: passes (corr_ref 0.7068). A frequency offset of 1e-5 (0.48 Hz) is caught (corr_ref 0.658), so only drifting rotations are detected. The complex figures were computed offline from the captured symbols, against the complex sequence the build script reproduces (numpy seed 0).
findings.suggested_fix: Compare against the complex transmitted symbols, phase-sensitively. Extend oracles.corr_ref to accept a complex reference (for example 'ref' as [re, im] pairs, or a separate 'ref_imag') and add an option such as 'phase': 'fixed' that scores Re(vdot)/(|r||x|) instead of |vdot|/(|r||x|). With that, the reference scores about 0.999, the 90-degree rotation about 0, the 45-degree rotation 0.71 and the conjugate about 0.04; a threshold of e.g. 0.95 then works. Add mutants for the rotation and the conjugate. If the team would rather accept a constant rotation (as gbf-dev-10 does for BPSK), reword the instruction instead: drop 'without rotation' and 'each sitting on its QPSK point', and correct the check note and spec_properties.symbol_sequence.

findings.claim: The instruction describes the repaired receiver as 'a Polyphase Clock Sync matched to the transmitter (same root-raised-cosine pulse and symbol rate, 32 filters, loop bandwidth 0.0628, maximum rate deviation 0.5)'. Written like that, these read as requirements, but none of them is checked (spec_properties.pulse_shape says 'not separately ... stated for context'). Variant v3 even uses a 64-filter bank, so a variant the gates count as correct contradicts the instruction.
findings.evidence: variants/v3_64_filter_bank.grc sets filter_size 64 and taps for 64 filters, and it passes V6 (gates.json). The oracle policy requires every stated requirement to be checked, and requires variants to satisfy the instruction. Two genuinely different alternatives keep 32 filters and pass 16/16 runs at 8 in parallel with bit-identical V6 values: the textbook taps form firdes.root_raised_cosine(nfilts, nfilts, 1.0/float(spb), rolloff, int(11*spb*nfilts)) (probes/alt_canonical_taps_int.grc), and spb = samp_rate/sym_rate/interpratio = 5.01, which compensates the clock offset (probes/alt_spb_5.01_compensated.grc).
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the receiver's 32 filters, loop bandwidth and maximum deviation from the instruction, keeping 'a Polyphase Clock Sync with root-raised-cosine filters matched to the transmitter', so that v3 stays valid; or keep the numbers, replace v3 with one of the two 32-filter alternatives above, and add block_present params checks for filter_size, loop_bw and max_dev.

compliance.verdict: The item passes every gate and most compliance checks, but its mutation gate overstates how much of the instruction the oracle covers: one medium and one low finding. I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates on 18 Oct: all five gates pass and gates.json is identical to the stored one (solvability 10/10, 975 tokens, 4/4 variants reach V6, start fails at V3 = fault.expected_rung, 15/15 mutants valid and killed). A copy of build.py run in scratch regenerates task.json, reference.grc, start.grc and all four variants byte for byte. Split discipline holds: the seed digital/demod/pam_timing.grc is 'test' in splits/flowgraph_seed_split.json, and its sha256 (95f77f48...) matches the installed example and source.sha256. No other first-set item uses this seed. gbf-dev-10 also has a Polyphase Clock Sync, but it differs in seed, fault (type_mismatch), modulation and split, so it is not a near-duplicate. The id, directory and split agree. The licence (GPL-3.0-or-later), source, cluster_id (= seed path), provenance (drafted_by Claude) and review (pending-team-review) fields are correct. The perturbation record matches the seed (32000, 4.2563, .35, time_bw 0, interpratio 1, noise 0, num_samps 10000000, rrate spb, max_dev 1.5) and lists every change. No model-visible file contains the canary, and the ± signs are stored as UTF-8. reports/reference/training_task_specs.json has no timing-recovery, Polyphase Clock Sync, samples-per-symbol or undefined-variable task, so the disjointness note is accurate. All 15 listed mutants break the spec, reach V5 and are killed in every run (4.8 and 4.9: 0/16 passes). The tolerances max_abs 2.5 and rms 5 % are the instruction's own numbers; corr_ref 0.67 is 95 % of the maximum possible with in-phase signs only. Scratch outputs are in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-17/ (regen/, aug_gate/, probes/).

findings.claim: The mutation gate passes only because the mutant list contains no mutant for the stated requirements the oracle cannot check (item-quality F1 and F2). Five obvious spec-breaking one-parameter mutants survive. All of them can be written with the existing set_param op and all reach V5. With them added, the gate fails (kill rate 0.75, below the 0.90 threshold).
findings.evidence: I appended 5 mutants to a scratch copy of the regenerated task (~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-17/aug_gate/) and ran ./gb tier-f gates on it. Mutation result: valid_mutants 20, kill_rate 0.75, passed false. Survivors: noise_amp 0 (the instruction says noise voltage 0.05); interpratio 1 and 1.002 (timing offset 0.998); rolloff 0.35 (roll-off 0.5); channels_channel_model_0 taps 1j (without rotation; keep the channel model). Three more violations also survive but cannot be written with the current edit ops: deleting four of the five File Sinks, inserting a rotation, and inserting a conjugate.
findings.suggested_fix: After fixing the oracle (item-quality F1/F2), add these five mutants to task.json (breaks: channel / pulse_shape / symbol_sequence). Add a sink-deletion mutant and a rotation mutant too; these need delete_block and insert_block ops in edit.py. Then re-run the gates.

findings.claim: Some of the item's recorded claims, which the team will read during its review, are wrong. (a) The corr_ref note and spec_properties.symbol_sequence say rotations are detected; constant rotations are not (item-quality F2). (b) spec_properties.pulse_shape says '64 filters ... give the same recovered symbols'. That holds only for the clock sync's own filter count. Changing the shared nfilts variable to 64 breaks the transmitter, because the Polyphase Arbitrary Resampler keeps its own Number of Filters at the default 32 while its taps are now designed for 64. (c) The build.py design note says spb = 4.99 'failed 1 run in 16'; that cannot be reproduced now.
findings.evidence: (b) probes/nfilts_64_tx_rx.grc fails V6 with corr_ref 0.071, max_abs 5.36 and rms 2.83 (filter_pfb_arb_resampler.block.yml: nfilts default '32'). (c) spb = samp_rate/sym_rate*interpratio (4.99) passed 64 of 64 runs (16 + 48, 8 in parallel), all with bit-identical V6 values (probes/probe_results_reps16.json, probe_results_reps48_499.json).
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the corr_ref note and spec_properties.symbol_sequence along with item-quality F2. In pulse_shape, write 'a 64-filter receiver bank (Polyphase Clock Sync filter_size 64 with matching taps)'. Update or drop the 4.99 sentence in build.py's design notes; the choice of 0.998 over 1.002 does not depend on it.
